@graph.name: How AC Repair Works in Charleston, SC

step.name: Same-Day Dispatch
step.text: When you call, our team dispatches a NATE-certified technician to your Charleston-area home. Most homeowners see a technician within 2 hours of calling, with same-day service available for calls placed before 2 PM.

step.name: Complete System Diagnostic
step.text: Your technician performs a comprehensive diagnostic that includes checking refrigerant levels and pressure, testing electrical connections and capacitors, evaluating airflow through the evaporator and condenser coils, inspecting thermostat calibration, and checking the condensate drain for blockages.

step.name: Honest Diagnosis and Upfront Pricing
step.text: Before any wrench turns, we explain the problem in plain language and give you a written estimate. If repair costs approach the threshold where AC replacement makes more financial sense, we tell you that too. We provide upfront flat-rate pricing before we start.

step.name: Repair and Verification
step.text: We complete the repair using manufacturer-specified parts, then run a full system verification. We check temperature differential across the evaporator coil, verify refrigerant charge, and confirm the system cycles properly before we leave your home. You get a written summary and a warranty on parts and labor.

mainEntity.name: How much does AC repair cost in Charleston, SC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most AC repairs in Charleston cost between $150 and $650. Capacitor replacement runs $150–$300. Refrigerant recharge (including leak detection) runs $250–$600 depending on the refrigerant type and charge required — R-410A costs have risen significantly since the January 2025 production ban. Compressor repair or replacement can reach $1,200–$2,500. We provide upfront flat-rate pricing after diagnosis, before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Why is my AC running but not cooling my Charleston home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common causes are low refrigerant from a leak, a dirty evaporator or condenser coil, a failing compressor, or ductwork leaks dumping cooled air into your attic. In Charleston's humidity, a clogged air filter alone can freeze the evaporator coil and shut down cooling within hours. Check your filter first. If it's clean and the system still isn't cooling, call for a diagnostic.

mainEntity.name: Do you repair AC systems in Charleston's historic homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We regularly service homes in the Historic District, Harleston Village, Wagener Terrace, and other pre-1950s neighborhoods where pier-and-beam foundations, original ductwork, and plaster walls create repair challenges that standard residential HVAC companies aren't prepared for.

mainEntity.name: My AC system uses R-410A. Is it still worth repairing in Charleston?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the repair and the system age. The EPA's R-410A production ban took effect January 2025, which has increased refrigerant recharge costs. Minor repairs remain cost-effective on any system. For refrigerant leak repairs or compressor replacement on older R-410A systems, we will give you the current numbers and help you decide whether repair or replacement makes more financial sense.
